key_insight: A Lagrangian view of 2D annular Rayleigh–Bénard convection reveals that FTLE ridges, flow curvature, and sliding-window kinematic measures can diagnose plumes, rolls, heat transport, and boundary-layer thickness in a unified way.
engineering_relevance: The proposed diagnostics offer a physics-informed toolkit for tracking coherent structures and heat-transfer transitions in convective systems, which is useful for thermal management and buoyancy-driven flow analysis.
method: Computed Finite-Time Lyapunov Exponent (FTLE) fields to identify plume-like transport structures.
Used flow curvature to characterize coherent swirling motion inside convective rolls.
Applied a sliding-window approach to finite-time kinematic measures and related them to Nusselt number and radial boundary-layer estimates.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a comprehensive parameter sweep and validation of the FTLE-based boundary-layer criterion against a classical Eulerian method, along with observed correspondence to Nusselt-number changes.
watch_item: The diagnostics are developed and validated for a 2D annular geometry, so transfer to fully 3D or strongly nonideal flows may require re-tuning and additional validation.
paper_title: A Lagrangian analysis of coherent structures in 2D annular Rayleigh-Bénard convection
